evidence: Verg. G. 4.176: sī parva licet compōnere magnīs
Cic. Rep. 1.26: quam parva sit terra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Small in size, amount or age: parvī are little children, and ā parvīs is “from childhood” (Cic. Leg. 2.9, Lewis & Short). Of a grown person’s height classical prose does not use parvus (Lewis & Short). Very small is parvulus (see tiny); smaller is minor (see less), smallest minimus (see least).

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.20.24: corporis exiguī, of slight build (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Small in measure: barely enough, or slight of build.

phrases.latin: dextrae sē parvus Iūlus implicuit sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs
phrases.english: little Iulus took my right hand and followed his father with shorter steps

phrases.latin: parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum: ā cane nōn magnō saepe tenētur aper
phrases.english: a small viper kills a huge bull with its bite; a boar is often held by a dog that is not big
